 ATP Finals ATP Finals tennis: Carlos Alcaraz v Ben Shelton – live semi-final updates
 🎾 ATP Finals updates from the last four in Turin
 🎾 Mail Katy | Men’s $350m prize money boost 
 LIVE  Updated  3m ago Katy Murrells Sat 21 Nov 2026 09.08 EST First published on Sat 21 Nov 2026 07.30 EST Share Key events 2h ago Preamble 
 Spain's Carlos Alcaraz reacts as he struggles during the first set. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters View image in fullscreen Spain's Carlos Alcaraz reacts as he struggles during the first set. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters Katy Murrells Sat 21 Nov 2026 09.08 EST First published on Sat 21 Nov 2026 07.30 EST Share Key events 2h ago Preamble 
 4m ago 09.06 EST First set: Alcaraz 2-4 Shelton* (*denotes next server) 
 15-0, 30-0, 40-0. Alcaraz’s most comfortable service game so far, by some distance. Shelton should really make some inroads in the next rally, but his forehand clatters into the net. Alcaraz holds to love; maybe that’ll rouse him into action.
 View image in fullscreen Alcaraz reacts. Photograph: Marco Bertorello/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.08 EST 6m ago 09.04 EST First set: Alcaraz* 1-4 Shelton (*denotes next server) 
 Shelton has landed nine out of 11 first serves so far, and it’s a similar story here. 15-0, 30-0, 40-0. And then Shelton’s second serve secures the game, when Alcaraz’s return skids long. Alcaraz played it safe with his movement against Cobolli yesterday, and tried to avoid sliding and running too much, but he doesn’t have that luxury today, given the way Shelton is smoking that ball.
 Share 10m ago 09.01 EST First set: Alcaraz 1-3 Shelton* (*denotes next server) 
 An Alcaraz ace may get the Spaniard going … but he’s a sitting target at the net on the next point and Shelton swats away a passing winner. The Alcaraz camp look concerned; meanwhile Juan Carlos Ferrero, Alcaraz’s former longtime coach who is now in Shelton’s corner, must be delighted, even though his face is betraying no emotion. 15-all becomes 40-15 … but some uncharacteristic errors from Alcaraz follow and it’s deuce. Alcaraz’s body language looks more positive when an inside-out forehand winner brings up his advantage … and he ends the game as he started it, with an ace. He’s finally on the board.
 Share Updated at  09.04 EST 15m ago 08.55 EST First set: Alcaraz* 0-3 Shelton (*denotes next server) 
 That’s the first time Alcaraz has been broken this tournament. There’s almost a stunned silence in the crowd; this isn’t the start they were expecting. And Shelton takes care of his serve to 15, to back up the break. Alcaraz still hasn’t won a game.
 View image in fullscreen Shelton stretches to return to Alcaraz. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP Share Updated at  09.01 EST 17m ago 08.53 EST Shelton breaks: Alcaraz 0-2 Shelton* (*denotes next server) 
 Shelton started slowly against Zverev in the group stage, getting broken in his opening service game, so he’ll be pleased to get his side of the scoreboard moving here. Not that television viewers can see it; there must be a glitch because the score has disappeared from the screen. It’s 30-15, though, and then 30-all, when Alcaraz pulls the trigger on his forehand but fires out. And then a messy volley gives Shelton a break point! Alcaraz surged out of the blocks in all of his group matches, but that certainly isn’t the case here. And Shelton dodges Alcaraz’s body serve and rips a physics-defying 216kph forehand return winner down the line to secure the break!
 Share 23m ago 08.48 EST First set: Alcaraz* 0-1 Shelton (*denotes next server) 
 Signore e signori, Alcaraz won the toss and has elected to receive first … and Shelton starts as he absolutely doesn’t mean to go on with a double fault. Shelton makes amends on the next point to level at 15-all ... and then comes to the net, where he’s so adept, to take the third point. Shelton then gives Alcaraz’s hamstring a real workout, dragging the sliding Spaniard right and left, and Shelton smacks away a winner. 40-15. And an ace seals the game. That was faultless after the double fault.
 Share 28m ago 08.43 EST So who wins today? Well, so much depends on Alcaraz’s physical condition. If his hamstring doesn’t hinder him, he should win, given the heights he’s hit this week and during the past two months. His shot-making was devastating against Cobolli yesterday, when he deliberately kept the points short and sharp to protect his injury. First-strike tennis is Shelton’s forte, though, so expect plenty of indoor fireworks between these two showmen and explosive hitters. And being a left-hander, Shelton will hope his ferocious cross-court forehand can stretch Alcaraz on the backhand side and put pressure on that injured hamstring. Shelton’s biggest weapon, of course though, is his serve.
 Share 31m ago 08.40 EST As for the head-to-head, Alcaraz leads 4-1, with Shelton’s only victory coming in that US Open quarter-final in September. Alcaraz has beaten Shelton indoors twice before: in the Paris Masters final two weeks ago and at the Laver Cup in 2024.
 Share 32m ago 08.39 EST Here they come, Shelton ahead of Alcaraz , whose body is again being held together by heavy strapping on his left hamstring, tape on his right knee and a compression sleeve to protect his right wrist. As for the style notes, Alcaraz is in dark blue and neon yellow, Shelton has ditched his sleeveless early-career Rafa look and is wearing a green top and shorts.
 Share 39m ago 08.32 EST Route to the semi-final. Alcaraz has been imperious so far, summed up by Tiafoe telling Alcaraz at one point during their group match that it was just all too much. Shelton, unlike Alcaraz, has experienced defeat this week, losing to Zverev in straight sets in a repeat of their US Open final, but he recovered to beat Jodar and book his spot in the semi-finals for the first time.
 Alcaraz
 beat Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2
 beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4
 beat Flavio Cobolli 6-4, 6-1
 Shelton
 beat Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3
 lost to Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6
 beat Rafael Jodar 7-6, 7-5
 Share 44m ago 08.27 EST Arévalo is jumping for joy, quite literally, after winning the match tie-break alongside Pavic for a 7-6 (10), 6-7 (7), 10-7 victory . So the Salvadoran-Croatian duo are back into the final, having finished runners-up in 2024. It’s still been a brilliant year for Skupski and Harrison, winning two grand slam titles in their first season together … and they’re all ushered off court rather unceremoniously because there’s the matter of Alcaraz v Shelton to be getting on with.
 Share 55m ago 08.16 EST In the first of the doubles semi-finals, Britain’s Neal Skupski and his American partner Christian Harrison , the reigning Australian and US Open champions, are into a deciding match tie-break against Marcelo Arévalo and Mate Pavic. Meanwhile away from the main court the Italian spectators are battling for position, because Alcaraz, just as he did yesterday, is currently out practising very close to his match, probably because he wants to stay warm and not risk his dodgy hamstring seizing up before he gets under way against Shelton in about 15 minutes’ time.
 Share 1h ago 08.07 EST Share 1h ago 08.04 EST The other semi-final takes place tonight, and it’s Alexander Zverev v Daniil Medvedev, after Medvedev, playing like it’s 2023/2024 again, beat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 6-4 in their winner-takes-all group match last night. It’s been a resurgent season for the Russian, having won four titles and broken back into the world’s top five, but he’ll be the underdog against Zverev, who has silenced some of the murmurs around his world No 1 status this week with three assured wins. Zverev and Alcaraz are very much the players to beat.
 Share 1h ago 07.53 EST And some more to keep you going … 
 Share 2h ago 07.30 EST Preamble
 Buongiorno ! Only two months after Carlos Alcaraz’s comeback tournament ended with a five-set, 3.33am defeat by Ben Shelton in the US Open quarter-finals – and only two weeks after Alcaraz gained some revenge over the American in the Paris final – the pair are at it again, this time for a spot in the ATP Finals, erm, final (maybe we should go back to the days of calling it the Masters Cup).
 Since losing to Shelton in New York , in a modern classic that ended with the dethroning of the champion and a coming-of-age victory for the eventual runner-up, Alcaraz has looked like a man determined to make up for those four months he missed with his wrist injury. His late-season charge includes a 20-1 win record, three titles and A+++ form this week despite a hamstring problem, topping his group with a perfect record of three straight-sets wins. He may have only one fit leg (and even that one has some tape on it too), but no one has been able to get near him.
 So where does this leave Shelton’s chances of reaching the season-ending final for the first time? His form has been more mixed than Alcaraz’s this tournament, with a loss to Alexander Zverev bookended by wins over Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar, but he does have an ace in his pack today in the form of Juan Carlos Ferrero, Alcaraz’s former coach who, after their surprise split at the end of last year, joined Shelton’s team this month.
 It’ll be fascinating to see if Ferrero makes any tweaks to Shelton’s tactics against a player Ferrero knows like no other, having coached Alcaraz to six of his seven slam titles … and also how Alcaraz deals with having such a familiar face in the opposite corner. If Alcaraz’s hamstring holds up, we could be in for another blockbuster in this late-season trilogy (hopefully without the 3.33am finish).
 Play begins at: about 1.30pm GMT/2.30pm Turin time.
 In the meantime: here’s some pre-match entertainment …
